**Test image observations:**
- Mango leaf (elongated, narrow shape)
- Leaf is mostly green with **irregular notching/scalloping along the leaf margins** (edges are jagged/chewed)
- Several small **reddish-brown spots** scattered on the leaf surface
- No white powdery coating, no dark sooty deposits, no galls, no dieback at tip

**Analysis:**
- The jagged/notched leaf margins are the key feature — this is characteristic of **Cutting_Weevil** damage, where adult weevils cut semicircular notches along leaf edges
- The small reddish-brown spots could be secondary damage
- Sooty_Mould (reference viewed) shows dark blackish/grey fungal coating — not present here
- No white powder (rules out Powdery_Mildew), no dark cankers (rules out Bacterial_Canker/Die_Back), no gall-like structures (rules out Gall_Midge), no anthracnose lesions with concentric rings

The irregular serrated/notched leaf margins are the hallmark symptom of cutting weevil feeding damage.
